sources.title: FDA Approves First Treatment to Reduce Risk of Serious Heart Problems Specifically in Adults with Obesity or Overweight
supports: supporting trial enrolled more than 17,600 participants
major adverse cardiovascular events 6.5% with Wegovy versus 8.0% with placebo
sources.limits: Indication is for adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity; do not generalize the cardiovascular outcome to all GLP-1 users.

sources.title: FDA Approves First Medication for Obstructive Sleep Apnea
supports: Zepbound approval for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity
first drug treatment option for that population
two randomized trials totaling 469 adults without type 2 diabetes
sources.limits: Population- and indication-specific approval; does not establish pharmacotherapy as a universal replacement for PAP or other OSA treatment.

sources.title: Novo Nordisk Annual Report 2025 — Commercial execution
supports: 2025 obesity-portfolio sales growth of 31% at constant exchange rates
3.6 million people reached with obesity medicines
Wegovy available in 52 countries by end of 2025
sources.limits: Issuer-reported commercial figures; primary for Novo Nordisk's own disclosures but interested evidence for competitive interpretation.

sources.title: Novo Nordisk stock decline as Eli Lilly gains GLP-1 market share
sources.limits: Point-in-time financial reporting; valuation and market-share figures move with the market and should always be dated.

sources.title: Eli Lilly hits $1 trillion market value, a first in health care
sources.limits: Single-company valuation milestone and point-in-time market reporting.

sources.title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Obesity without Diabetes (SELECT)
supports: 20% relative reduction in the primary cardiovascular composite
sources.limits: Trial population restricted to people with overweight or obesity and pre-existing cardiovascular disease without diabetes; not generalizable to all GLP-1 users.

sources.title: Bariatric surgeries on the decline as use of GLP-1 drugs rises
sources.publisher: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, covering JAMA Surgery (Oct. 2024)
sources.limits: Correlational; insurance, post-pandemic elective-surgery patterns, and other confounders remain plausible.

sources.title: What to know about the BALANCE model for GLP-1s in Medicare and Medicaid
supports: evolving federal pricing and coverage policy
sources.limits: Policy-landscape summary; coverage rules can change and should be rechecked before publication.
